title: Expand "Hide other windows when hovering over tooltips"'s hoverable area into the entire window preview area
line: With "Hide other windows when hovering over tooltips" on, the window now stays highlighted while hovering its title, close button and media controls in the task tooltip, not only its thumbnail.
explanation: Each tooltip entry highlighted its window from a HoverHandler on the thumbnail only; the header had its own handler, but it was only enabled with thumbnails off. So with thumbnails on, moving onto the title, close button or the player and volume rows ended the highlight and the other windows came back. The change moves the highlighting to one passive HoverHandler on the whole entry (header and thumbnail handlers keep only their visual hover state). In a group tooltip, the media rows only count when that window's title has the track, because otherwise the controls sit on the first entry without necessarily belonging to its window (the concern Christoph Wolk raised in e47d6d64c9).

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: Highlight the window over its whole tooltip entry

With thumbnails on, the window was only highlighted while hovering its
thumbnail, so moving to the title, close button or media controls
brought the other windows back. Track hover on the whole entry instead.

BUG: 528348

media.caption: Pointer on the tooltip's title ("Dolphin / Home"): Konsole comes back in front, no highlight.
Pointer on the same title: Dolphin stays highlighted and Konsole stays hidden.
Thumbnail → title → thumbnail → media controls: the highlight only holds over the thumbnail.
Same path: the highlight holds over the title and the media controls too.

review.text: Moving window-highlight tracking to a single passive HoverHandler on ToolTipInstance cleanly keeps the hovered window highlighted across the title, close button, and media controls without breaking button clicks or existing visual hover highlights. The grouped-tooltip Y-position guard properly avoids highlighting an arbitrary first window when hovering media/volume controls that do not belong to it, respecting prior maintainer feedback. Before/after screenshots and video clearly demonstrate the fix.

reviews.text: Moving window-highlight tracking to a single passive HoverHandler on ToolTipInstance cleanly keeps the hovered window highlighted across the title, close button, and media controls without breaking button clicks or existing visual hover highlights. The grouped-tooltip Y-position guard properly avoids highlighting an arbitrary first window when hovering media/volume controls that do not belong to it, respecting prior maintainer feedback. Before/after screenshots and video clearly demonstrate the fix.

Moves the windowsHovered() call from the thumbnail-only (or header-only without thumbnails) HoverHandlers to one HoverHandler on the whole ToolTipInstance, so the title, close button and media/volume rows keep the window highlighted, which is exactly what the reporter asked; the per-part handlers keep only their visual highlight. The group-tooltip exclusion of media rows that may not belong to that entry (point.position.y vs playerController/volumeControls y, unless titleIncludesTrack) is a careful answer to the concern in e47d6d64c9, and the thumbnails-off path still works through the same handler. Before/after screenshots and video frames show Konsole returning over the title and media row on master and staying hidden with the patch. Small, right layer, no lifetime or binding hazards beyond what the old handlers already had.
